html:
SMTO-CTR-0001 — Task contract generation failed

GUID: 2ec4f714-ee81-4171-b10d-61a154fb636c
Slug: task-contract-failed
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't turn your request into a Task Contract, the checked plan it writes before doing any work. It didn't act on this version of your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Task contract step under the task and read the section Why this attempt was rejected. It names the real cause, such as the model service failing or the model's answer being cut off or unreadable.
  2. If the reason is about the model service, ask the person who manages SMTO to check the model settings under Settings › Setup. Retrying won't help while the model SMTO uses to write the plan can't be reached or keeps failing.
  3. Select Retry on the task, or Retry contract generation in the Task contract step. Retry writes the plan again from the same request using this task's saved settings.
  4. If it fails again for the same reason, rewrite your request more clearly and send it as a new message instead of retrying unchanged. Sending the same request with the same problem again will usually fail the same way.

What success looks like

  • The Task contract step shows Task contract generated and the task starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Task Contract Integrity Guard to get the task through; it blocks plans that reach beyond what you asked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Task Contract compiler rejected or failed the attempt (cause-specific reason when known, otherwise a generic compilation failure), so no actions were authorized for this revision.

What this means

  • Task Contract failure handling records the compiler's rejected attempt and selects a cause-specific message when known, otherwise its generic compilation failure. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Task Contract failure handling records the compiler's rejected attempt and selects a cause-specific message when known, otherwise its generic compilation failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the saved attempt reason, transport/output evidence and revision_execution_started rather than inferring a bad user request.

How to fix it

  • Open the failed attempt in the task's Task contract activity and read 'Why this attempt was rejected' (reason, transport and output evidence). Correct that cause, then retry with the task's Retry control, which reuses the task's saved policy; never bypass the Integrity Guard to accept broadened scope.
  • Inspect the failed Task Contract attempt and compile again from the original request. Correct the recorded compiler cause; do not bypass integrity checks to accept broadened scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported explicit compiler attempt accepts the intended source revision with earlier execution receipts preserved.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
